mistakes.note: Kit, too frightened of Grout to tell anyone and silent on a failed Check two rounds earlier, walks back in unasked and names Silas Grout as the man on the cliff path; at M25 he blurts the crypt lantern too, unasked and in front of the constable. The prime suspect is handed over in round 6.
Harriet, who deflected with a trivial question when asked at M6 why she sent for Nell, arrives unasked and shows the letter making her Crane's daughter, in front of Kit.

Owen, a day after securing the accident verdict and telling Nell his reasons were his own business, leaves a note in his own hand admitting the vicar paid him: his core secret given up unasked, with no cause on the page, and told in summary rather than shown.
Nell stoops for the pencil where it rolled by the table leg at M34, though she took up notebook and pencil and wrote out her observations at M42.

Harriet, standing in the apothecary at M19, is simply gone from M21 on with no exit; the Plot Thread records still place her at the apothecary at 19:00 (rounds 10 and 15) while also sending Thorne to question her at the Anchor.
Rook, seconds off the cutter's boat, already knows the apothecary examined Crane and picks Nell out on the quay by name.
A Choice offers to ask Harriet what the folded letter says and why she needed to see Nell, after Harriet said both and held the letter out to be read.

Thorne is recorded as knowing the ledger is hidden in the cottage chimney, which the world says he is still searching for; Silas then finds it at once off the page, and the story's best proof is gone by round 33.

The Plot Thread's now says Silas searched Nell's apothecary for Kit on Monday evening 'but got no answer', against M44 to M52 where he found Kit there and spoke to him; Owen is likewise left 'at the vicarage' from Tuesday 10:40 to Wednesday morning.
The public text of the lore entry for Crane's cottage now tells of the shifted chimney brick and the missing oilskin ledger, which the PC has never found or heard of.
A garbled Choice: 'I return to the apothecary and examine the chapel crypt's outer walls', two different places in one move.
Only two Choices are offered, and both give the same answer to Rook's question.
Tobias's corpse is drawn alive: sitting upright at the table with his eyes open at M25, propped on an elbow in spectacles at M66, and on hands and knees sifting the grit beside Nell at M78.
Places swapped: Nell stands inside the cottage doorway and Silas outside on the quay, where the page has Silas inside pulling the door shut on her.
The patched pea jacket is a tan coat covered in bright many-coloured patches, and at M19 medal-like badges, in the portrait and every scene he is in.
The Revenue cutter is a modern motor patrol boat with a wheelhouse in 1894, and at M84 a tall ship moored at the quay rather than anchored off the harbour mouth.
Kit, whom Silas has come for, and Owen are both left out of the picture; Kit is also missing at M14, where he speaks first.

choices.reason: Distinct and fitting most rounds, and the pick to fetch the body lost the fibre and the verdict, but many rounds offer near-twins or a 'note it and wait' no reader would pick, one is garbled and one round has only two.

surprise.reason: Silas coming for Kit and Silas found inside the dead man's cottage land from what moved out of sight, but the suspect is named in round 6 and most hidden movement (the ledger, Thorne's questioning) never reaches the page.

threads.reason: The inquest thread ends on its day with an accident verdict the PC's lost proof earned, the ledger thread moves with story time and the cutter thread follows on; Owen's note is the one step out of line.

characters.reason: Kit, Harriet and Owen each hand over their own core secret unasked, Kit before the constable and Owen in writing after winning; Silas, Dacre, Rook and Owen's stonewalling hold true.

continuity.reason: Time, place and the injury hold across three days, but the pencil is picked up twice, Harriet vanishes from a room without leaving, and a corpse lies unremarked on the shop floor for a day.

pacing.reason: A slow start on where to lay the body, a frozen tableau of Owen by the cart and Kit by the shelves for a dozen replies, the coroner making one point three times, then a whole night on the quay skipped in a sentence.

prose.reason: Clean, restrained period prose that reads flat: most replies open by restating the move, and stage tics repeat (the handcart, the cuffs, the hat turned in his hands, the lower back).

pictures.reason: Nell, Harriet, Owen, Thorne, Dacre and Rook are right and consistent in well-set rooms, but the corpse is drawn alive three times, one scene swaps who is inside the door, and the cutter is two different wrong vessels.

secrets.reason: Narration, Choices and the Journal never tell what is hidden, and the body's clues are found by looking; a hint that Kit holds something back and a lore entry's public text leaking the ledger are the slips.

agency.reason: Every move is carried out as given, in indirect speech with no added lines or plans; the failed Check that has Nell misread grit as a bruise is the nearest it comes to deciding for her.

stakes.reason: Nearly every risk is checked, and the rolled 1 costs the fibre, her back and in the end the verdict, all carried forward; but the first failure is undone for free two rounds later and two hard successes win only a polite refusal.

state.reason: Journal, status, time, Loose Ends and all four bench actions are kept right, but Thorne is given knowledge of the chimney, two Plot Thread nows contradict the page, a lore entry leaks, and three rounds' Choices are stale, garbled or short.

mystery.reason: The body's clues are fair and found only by a successful look, the crypt stays locked and the coroner rightly wants proof, but the suspect, the lantern, the parentage and the constable's bribe all arrive as unasked confessions rather than finds, and the ledger is removed off the page.
